data.content_ref: inline:The target explicitly answers only the resilience-versus-redundancy half of the problem and never addresses the problem's second, equally central requirement: to 'identify what evidence would distinguish failure modes that are truly independent from failures that merely appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found.' The closest it comes are analogy transfer_claims stating that observing P(A∩B)≈P(A)P(B) under normal operation is 'weak evidence' and that the burden is to show no hidden common cause. But those are assertions about why a particular evidentiary standard is weak, not the requested identification of discriminating evidence. It offers no concrete evidentiary test or observable signature (e.g., cross-time covariance before/after a shared-cause event, substrate-diversity controls, conditional independence given substrate held fixed, or post-mortem co-failure clustering) that would distinguish genuine independence from latent-correlation-until-triggered. The counterconditions mention mitigations (mandatory multi-cloud) and a collapse condition (shared external infra), but still do not state evidence that would distinguish the two failure-mode classes. Since this distinguishing-evidence requirement is a named objective of the problem (not out-of-scope elaboration), its absence is a genuine substantive gap.
